messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE fired — p99 latency breach for model-serving.us-west (> 1.2s for 5m). PagerDuty: https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC12345

sarah: Acked. I'm oncall — investigating.

sarah: Quick look at the dashboard: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~2.1s. Error rate normal. Link: https://grafana.example.com/d/abc/model-serving-tail

michael: Noting a rollout around 02:10 UTC that toggled the batcher change (disable prefix cache for long sequences). Could be correlated.

jen: tagging infra — any autoscale/queueing alerts?

ops-bot: autoscaler reports no new scale events in last 30m; queue length spiked for 30s windows.

michael: Deploy details: release/4567 -> model-serving v2.3, batcher=v2. Change set includes `no-prefix-cache-for-long` flag.

sarah: Can we rollback the flag quickly? If we revert, we should mitigate tail while root cause is investigated.

michael: I can revert the flag. Two quick options:
```
# option A: flip env on deployment
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-serving BATCHER_MODE=legacy

# option B: rollback the release
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/model-serving --to-revision=4566
```

sarah: Option A seems safest for fast rollback. Michael, go for it and post status.

michael: Applying now.

deploy-bot: started rollout of env change for deploy/model-serving (namespace: inference) by michael.

michael: done, env var set. Restarting pods to pick up change.

deploy-bot: pods restarting (3/3).

sarah: Observing metric tail... p99 dropping to ~650ms. Good sign.

kevin: I'm seeing tokenizer service CPU climb — looks like several very large sequence requests landed. Might be hitting tokenization stage and causing backend stalls. Suggest adding a quick ingress request-size limiter rule (rate-limit / max-tokens) while we stabilize.

jen: If we need to apply a traffic rule, prefer a temporary header-based route for new users only. We don't want to throttle existing customers.

michael: Also noticed KV cache evictions spike coincident with the rollout — long sequences blow out prefix hits. I'll temporarily increase cache TTL to reduce churn: `kubectl exec -n infra -c redis cache-0 -- redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru && redis-cli CONFIG SET timeout 10` (doing safe change).

rebecca: Support: no major customer-facing outages yet; a couple of retries from ACME Corp's ingestion pipeline, they are watching. I'm pinging CS to proactively notify.

sarah: PD incident updated: acknowledged by sarah. Adding owners: michael (runtime), kevin (platform).

michael: Cache TTL patched. Monitoring.

sarah: p99 now ~320ms, p95 ~280ms. We're approaching normal. Keeping the page open for 15 more minutes.

rebecca: FYI I opened a low-priority ticket with ACME support to confirm no data loss.

kevin: I pushed a temporary LB rule to reject requests with token-count > 100k with 429 and a clear body so clients can retry smaller chunks. Command: `routectl apply -f tmp/limit-large-requests.yaml`

sarah: Nice. We should still plan a postmortem to verify the rollout testing matrix missed long-sequence perf and cache churn. Assigning follow-up to michael + kevin.

michael: Agreed — will capture logs and a repro using the long-sequence harness.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 — status: acknowledged by sarah.

sarah: We're stable for 12m with no additional p99 spikes. Closing the page in 3m if no regressions. :thumbsup:

sarah: Closing the page now — metrics steady. Postmortem ticket created: PMT-789 (assigned: michael, kevin).

michael: thanks — will include suggested QA for long-input workloads + cache stress tests.

kevin: will follow up on ingress limits and an automated canary for batcher flag changes.

rebecca: looped CS and left ACME note.

sarah: Good job team.
